cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD's servant Moses had commanded it. Joshua built the altar "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). The text even says he built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses (Joshua 8:31). So this wasn't Joshua winging it like a man with no recipe, friends. He was following the instructions he'd been given.

The answer is uncut. The Book of the Law of Moses said, "an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used." (Joshua 8:31). Joshua built it according to what was written. Leaving things exactly as they are is hard for a stamper like me, friends, but Joshua pulled it off.

The answer is True. Joshua 8:31 says, "…on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings." Both kinds are named right there. The text says they built the altar according to what is written in the Book of the Law, and then they offered on it.

The answer is a copy of the law of Moses. Joshua "…inscribed on the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he had written." (Joshua 8:32). He did it right there with all the Israelites watching. That's a lot of words to put on stones, friends, so I hope he stretched his hand first.

The answer is False. Joshua 8:33 says, "All Israel, foreigners and citizens alike, with their elders, officers, and judges, stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" Foreigners and citizens alike were in that crowd. Everybody had a spot, friends.

The answer is bless. Moses had commanded it earlier, and the text states the purpose plainly: to bless the people of Israel (Joshua 8:33). Half stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, on both sides of the ark. That's a whole lot of standing for a good cause, bakers.

The answer is False. The text says Joshua "…read aloud all the words of the law—the blessings and the curses—according to all that is written in the Book of the Law." (Joshua 8:34). Blessings and curses both got read. He didn't pick only the nice parts, friends.

The answer is the women and the little ones. Joshua read "…before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who lived among them." (Joshua 8:35). The women and the little ones are named right there in the assembly, bakers. That's who else was listening.
